stories.title: Climate scientists urge US lawmakers to vote no on sweeping permitting bill
stories.summary: Open letter warns Baaja, intended to expedite energy and infrastructure projects, will cause irreversible climate harm A group of more than 120 climate scientists have urged US lawmakers to not pass contentious legislation to speed up the building of energy projects, datacenters and other infrastructure, amid a growing backlash to the sweeping permitting bill. In an open letter to members of the House of Representatives , the collection of Earth and social sciences researchers expressed “deep concern” that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (or Baaja) weakens environmental laws, locks in new fossil fuel projects without recourse and delivers only minor cuts to planet-heating emissions. stories.title: Democrat Victoria Broderick unseats eight-term Republican incumbent in Tennessee to win election
stories.summary: Victory expands Democrats’ House majority, its largest advantage in three decades Democrat Victoria Broderick has won Tennessee’s fourth congressional district, unseating eight-term Republican incumbent Scott DesJarlais in one of the biggest House upsets of the cycle. The victory expands Democrats’ historic House majority in the 120th Congress to 259 seats, the party’s largest advantage in three decades , and flips a seat that Donald Trump carried by more than 20 points in 2024. Broderick, 34, a former technology and logistics professional who previously ran for Congress in 2024, told the Guardian in an interview before her race was called that she connected with constituents who had not voted in years and met Republicans concerned about affordability who appreciated the “integrity” she brought to the race.
